title: Lesson 8: Virtual Memory & the TLB — js-tools
desc: Virtual-to-physical address translation through paging and multi-level page tables, what the MMU is and what a page table entry actually holds (present, read/write, no-execute and dirty bits), the cost of a page table walk, and the TLB that avoids it. Verified by running a hand-written engine: a 32-bit single-level page table costs exactly 4MB while a 48-bit space would need 256GB; a 2-level table costs only 8KB for 2MB of address space in use, 512 times cheaper; the first access to a page is a TLB miss and the next is a hit. Demo: translate virtual addresses live and compare page table sizes.
